rationale: Engineering managers at mid-to-large software companies are identifiable buyers who do pay for developer-productivity and CI/CD tooling (e.g., Datadog, LinearB, Swarmia), and test-bypass tracking is a real recurring pain. However, the total score falls just below the validate threshold, primarily because willingness to pay for a narrow test-bypass audit tool is uncertain (companies expect this in their existing CI platform), operational autonomy is limited (the product would need deep CI/CD integrations that require ongoing maintenance per platform), and the signal is a single forum post with no demand cluster. The idea needs stronger market evidence before warranting even a validate stage.
solution_plan: If validated later: WHAT: A CI/CD Test-Bypass Audit SaaS — a lightweight integration that monitors pipeline runs and flags when mandatory tests are skipped, producing a weekly report for engineering managers. BUILD: Claude + a webhook listener + a simple dashboard (or even just a weekly Slack/email digest) + Stripe; buildable with moderate integration work (GitHub Actions / GitLab CI webhooks). SELL: Engineering managers and platform leads at 50–500-person software companies via LinkedIn outreach and dev-productivity communities. MAINTAIN: Webhook ingestion and report generation run automatically; billing is Stripe self-serve. Human touch: approving outreach. However, do not invest in this until a demand cluster (3+ independent signals) is confirmed.
notes: Total 5.2 is below min_total_to_validate (5.5); staged drop. Failing gates if re-evaluated at build: operational_autonomy=5 < 7, willingness_to_pay=5 meets floor exactly.
